sentences.text: Qianxisaurus is classified as an extinct genus of pachypleurosaur or alternatively as a basal eosauropterygian.
The generic name includes the Greek word saûros, meaning 'lizard', while the specific name is derived from Chajiang, the town near which the specimen was collected.
The animal possesses a premaxilla with eight teeth.
The total estimated body length of the individual is over 80 cm.
Qianxisaurus shares a longitudinal groove on the upper-back-facing surface of its dorsal ribs exclusively with the basal pistosauroids Corosaurus, Sanchiaosaurus, Kwangsisaurus, and Chinchenia.
The species is known only from a single nearly complete and articulated holotype skeleton — the specimen the species is based on.
The skull of the holotype specimen measures 7.6 cm in length.
The holotype was discovered in 2006 near the Huangnihe River at Chajiang in southwestern Guizhou Province, most likely collected from the Zhuganpo Member of the Falang Formation.
The genus was first described and named by Yen-Nien Cheng, Xiao-Chun Wu, Tamaki Sato, and Hsi-Yin Shan in 2012.
The animal lived during the Middle Triassic (Ladinian age) in Guizhou Province, southwestern China, dating to the Ladinian stage of the late Middle Triassic, approximately 238 million years ago.
The time range for the genus is the Ladinian, from 241.464 to 237 million years ago.
